mechanism_narrative: The sharp recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT from t-2w to t-0w will continue to pull more weekday trips into the city center, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as commuting-linked purchases resume.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep rising for two more weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, reject the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains below -70 and WORKPLACES below -45, retail visitation will keep falling because access constraints and reduced commuting suppress discretionary shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -70 or WORKPLACES stays below -45 for a full week
evidence_refs: fact:mobility is still deeply negative but improving
failure_condition: Reject if TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay below the stated thresholds yet RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean within 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in RESIDENTIAL together with continued weakness in GROCERY_PHARM implies more staying-home substitution and fewer out-of-home retail trips, which should keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Reject if RESIDENTIAL remains above +15 and GROCERY_PHARM stays below -30 but RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to its last-4-week mean over 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week jump in PARKS toward less negative values signals warmer-weather outdoor activity, which should partially substitute for mall and restaurant shopping and cap RETAIL_REC in the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by at least 20 points week-on-week
failure_condition: Reject if PARKS improves by 20 points or more week-on-week and RETAIL_REC still rises above its last-4-week mean within 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: Once GROCERY_PHARM moves above -40, households are likely making more essential trips and combining them with nearby nonessential purchases, which will lift RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -55.7 to -35.9 over the last two weekly means
failure_condition: Reject if GROCERY_PHARM stays above -40 for a full week and RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL falls while WORKPLACES rises, time spent at home is being replaced by work-linked outside activity, and that shift should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks through more incidental shopping trips.
failure_condition: Reject if RESIDENTIAL declines and WORKPLACES rises for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC fails to beat its prior 4-week average over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT recovers faster than WORKPLACES, retail mobility will rise only modestly because commuting channels reopen before broader spending confidence returns; the signal is strongest in the first week after the crossover.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above WORKPLACES relative recovery by at least 10 points
failure_condition: Reject if TRANSIT outperforms WORKPLACES by 10 points or more but RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: During late-spring reopening, a continued narrowing of the gap between PARKS and RETAIL_REC means outdoor leisure is normalizing before shopping, so RETAIL_REC should keep improving over the next four weeks if park mobility stabilizes rather than surges further.
failure_condition: Reject if PARKS stabilizes near current levels but RETAIL_REC does not continue improving relative to the last 4 weeks over the next 28 days.
